answer retired the memory (I1: a RETIRED row is never returned as a belief).

ChangeEvent.description: One per ripple (ADR-0015); created in the trigger's transaction, appended per wave.
ChangeEvent.title: ChangeEvent

EventMemoryOut.description: A memory an event names: its text and its status now (RETIRED marks the past).

EventsOut.description: GET /events: newest first; `total` counts every event the user has.
EventsOut.title: EventsOut

ExportOut.description: Everything Ripple holds about the user (FR-15), including retired history.
ExportOut.title: ExportOut

ForgetEvent.description: Forget is deletion, not a state change, so it is logged apart from ChangeEvents (I7).
ForgetEvent.title: ForgetEvent

GraphOut.description:
The user's visible memories and the links between them, for the map page.

Same I1 boundary as GET /memories: RETIRED rows are absent, so links to them are
absent too; SUSPECT and PENDING_USER rows carry `flagged`.
GraphOut.title: GraphOut

ProfileAttributeOut.description: One attribute of the user's own facts, as the domain adapter declares it.

QuestionOut.description: One parked question (ripple.core.answers.PendingQuestion over the wire).
QuestionOut.title: QuestionOut

SourceOut.description:
Where a resume fact came from: the upload and, when the source_ref carries a

StructuredFact.description: subject / attribute / value, the part rules and the rule linker can read.

A new version created_by user that ripples as a user_edit (FR-12, ADR-0042).

The inspector names the memory, so there is nothing to detect: the write goes
straight to versioning rather than through change detection.
Hard deletion of the whole version chain and its depends_on subtree (I7).
